hook_form.value: Prediction hook (N-01): L1's temporal opener — 'Forty thousand years ago, a grandmother sings the road to the water: first verse, the big rock; second verse, the bent tree.' Read cold, the topic is graspable (an old woman singing directions to water, deep prehistory) and the completion is NOT predictable: the scene reads as colour; the payoff is that the song is a storage technology (L2 reveals the map, L7 names the tool). Payoff lines named: L2 (first reveal), L7 (plain payoff). Cold test: PASS. The click half is DR-E4-CLICK: title 'A Song Remembers What Words Forget.' + cover line 'A SONG IS A MAP.' (4 words, S-09) over the grandmother and children on the road between the big rock and the bent tree.

story_structure.value: Beat-sheet, lite (satisfaction + rhythm — a deliberate variation; a music episode should move in beats): opening image (the sung road) → theme (a song is a map) → catalyst (plain words fail) → low point (knowledge dying in scrambled lists) → finale (the tool is still in the viewer's own life). Villain (N-06), named: Words without a beat — plain spoken lists (consequence stack recorded: sequence is the first casualty; one swapped word silently changes the route; each retelling drifts further). Intended feeling: delight — the small shock of realising a song is a piece of technology. The ONE vivid detail (N-03): the grandmother singing the road to the water — first verse, the big rock; second verse, the bent tree.
